Portable Python · Technical Tutorial

One Folder, One Python Environment

Why does Python break when the path changes? Which approaches exist? How this repository makes relocation a default capability with a runtime plus a repair payload — and how to package cowsay yourself and run it from a new folder.

Windows / PowerShell 7 python-portable-win v1.4 15.1 MB example package No host Python required
01 Why it breaks 02 Approaches 03 How it works 04 Layout 05 Usage 06 cowsay walkthrough 07 Limits 08 Compiled code

01Why moving the folder breaks things

CPython derives sys.prefix from the location of python.exe, so the interpreter itself is inherently relocatable. What actually breaks are the artifacts that recorded absolute paths during installation.

Good

Interpreter and stdlib

Lib/, DLLs/, and site-packages are found relative to the executable, so they survive a move.

Bad

pip / uv launchers

Generated .exe files embed the absolute interpreter and script paths from install time. After a move they still point at the old location.

Bad

Environment and caches

User directories, Tcl/Tk init scripts, Jupyter kernelspecs, and editable installs all leak host paths.

Anatomy of a pip launcher

Installing cowsay 6.1 in a plain venv produces a 108,368-byte cowsay.exe. It is not a single program; it is a PE launcher with appended data. The executable part starts the interpreter, and the tail records which script to run.

Reading the tail of the exe confirms it (measured values):

Read appended tail dataActual output
total_bytes      108368
shebang_offset   108032
shebang_raw      b'#!C:\\Users\\user\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\launcher-demo\\venv\\Scripts\\python.exe\nPK\x03\x04...'
zip_offset       108107
zip_entries      ['__main__.py']

The zip payload contains a single __main__.py that forwards to the package entry point:

__main__.pyzip payload · 141 B
import sys
from cowsay.__main__ import cli
if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.argv[0] = sys.argv[0].removesuffix('.exe')
    sys.exit(cli())
After move

cowsay.exe

Fails silently: exit 1 with empty stdout and stderr. To the user it just "does nothing".

After move

python -m cowsay

Works normally. The interpreter, stdlib, and site-packages are intact; only the launcher is broken.

Extra evidence

pyvenv.cfg

The home, executable, and command lines also contain absolute paths.

That is the starting point for the repair strategy: do not change Python and do not scan user code — just regenerate the launchers. The shim approach moves entry information out of the binary tail into a readable .entry file, and paths are derived at runtime from the current location.

Four typical failure points

Launchers
Console-script .exe files embed a shebang or trampoline metadata. This is the most common failure and the easiest to misdiagnose as "the environment is broken".
sys.path
The official embeddable package pins search paths in python314._pth; by default it contains only the interpreter directory, not the current working directory.
Package manager
PEP 668's EXTERNALLY-MANAGED blocks system-level installs, while user-level installs write into %APPDATA%.
Tcl/Tk and data
init.tcl, Jupyter kernels, and editable .pth files may all record install-time paths.
The real issue is not "Python is not portable" but derived files created at install time are not portable. As long as they can be regenerated, the whole directory can move freely.

02Comparing existing approaches

These are the most common options. The conclusions are qualitative: no single approach delivers zero host dependency, relocation, continued development, and a small footprint at the same time.

Approach Isolation Relocation Keep developing Main cost
venv Medium: depends on host interpreter Partially; launchers and path caches break Good Target machine needs the same Python
conda-pack High Needs relocation scripts; prefix paths may remain Fair Large environments, conda ecosystem
Raw embeddable package High Interpreter moves fine Poor: no pip or full toolchain Manual ._pth edits, pip bootstrapping
PyInstaller High Output is relocatable No: source becomes a frozen program Antivirus false positives, dynamic import issues, hard debugging
uv python install + venv High venv still contains absolute paths Very good Target machine needs uv or an executable entry point
This repository High: never touches host state Launchers repair themselves Good: it is a normal interpreter You need to understand shims and repair triggers
Guidance

You only need a non-editable program

PyInstaller or Nuitka are more direct; the trade-off is losing "keep developing" and a small runtime footprint.

Guidance

You need to copy, run, and keep developing

This repository's model: one directory is an interpreter plus flat site-packages, and launchers heal themselves.

03How this repository solves it

The core idea is a split of responsibilities: the runtime layer owns the interpreter, package installs, launcher repair, and packaging; the orchestration layer belongs to the application and owns source staging, frontend builds, native DLLs, and smoke tests.

Engine choice

EngineSourceBenefitsConstraints
python-build-standalone (PBS) uv python install Full stdlib, bundled Tcl/Tk, headers and import libraries Larger; requires uv
Official embeddable python.org download Small, offline-friendly, pinned SHA256 No pip/Tk; ._pth restricts sys.path

Launcher repair: shim + entry

Every Scripts/*.exe generated by pip or uv is replaced by two things: a copy of shim.exe that contains no paths, and a sibling .entry text file. At runtime the shim derives the interpreter from its own location.

python\Scripts\cowsay.entryActual build output
module=cowsay.__main__
func=cli
gui=false

The same cowsay entry, two artifacts with very different size and path dependence:

pip launcher
108,368 B
shim + entry
7,213 B

The size is roughly 1/15; more importantly, the shim contains no paths at all. Entry information lives entirely in the readable .entry file.

Whether the folder moved is detected from the path marker in python/.portable_root. Every interpreter start compares the marker and rebuilds launchers on a mismatch, so repair happens even when the user double-clicks python.exe directly.

Install and verification

  • bootstrap.ps1 extracts the engine into python.new, verifies SHA256 against checksums.psd1, and only then swaps out the old python/.
  • The installed patch version is written to python/.portable_version and reused by later bootstraps that omit -Version, preventing version drift.
  • PBS mode removes EXTERNALLY-MANAGED because the interpreter belongs to this package and does not need PEP 668 protection.
  • pip.ps1 rejects --user and keeps pip/uv caches inside the package.

04Repository layout

All runtime logic lives in scripts/; applications only reference it. python/ is always generated output.

python-portable-win/v1.4
python-portable-win/
├── scripts/                     # runtime engine (core)
│   ├── bootstrap.ps1            # download / verify / install engine + pip + hook + shim
│   ├── activate.ps1             # inject PATH / Tcl / caches, repair launchers
│   ├── pip.ps1                  # isolated installs, repair right after install
│   ├── repair.py                # rebuild shims and .entry for this location
│   ├── sitecustomize.py         # self-check on interpreter start / exit
│   ├── workspace.ps1            # resolve -Workspace and stage runtime files
│   ├── build_release.ps1        # stream the workspace into a ZIP
│   └── new-portable-project.ps1 # scaffold: app / scripts / multi
├── templates/                   # scaffold templates
├── docs/zh · docs/en             # architecture and troubleshooting (Chinese default)
├── skills/portable-python-env/  # agent operating manual
├── hello/                       # example app
└── python/                      # generated, git-ignored
Runtime

scripts/

Install, activate, install packages, repair, package. The default workspace is scripts/..; -Workspace points it elsewhere.

Application

templates/ + app repo

The scaffold writes the app's own build-*.ps1; frontend builds, DLLs, and smoke tests stay in the application.

Convention

.portable/

The consumer project's output directory: python/, scripts/, app/, and dist/ are isolated there.

05How to use it

Local development: three commands

PowerShellRepository root
PS> .\scripts\bootstrap.ps1
PS> .\scripts\pip.ps1 install cowsay
PS> . .\scripts\activate.ps1
PS> cowsay -t "hello portable"

Activation is optional: without it, python\python.exe and python\Scripts\*.exe still work. Activation only injects the environment into the current shell and provides deactivate.

As a shared runtime

An application repository does not copy the runtime scripts; it consumes them as a submodule or pinned copy, and all generated files go into .portable/.

Consumer ModeAny app repository
PS> git submodule add https://github.com/ra9fael/python-portable-win.git vendor/python-portable-win
PS> .\vendor\python-portable-win\scripts\new-portable-project.ps1 `
        -ProjectRoot . -AppDir app -Requirements requirements.txt
PS> .\scripts\build-portable.ps1
Scaffold profileUse caseOutput
app (default)Single applicationsubmodule + scripts/build-portable.ps1 + root .portable/
scriptsPersonal portable script workspacecopied scripts/, no submodule, code in my_tools/
multiSeveral apps in one repositoryone scripts/build-<app>.ps1 and <app>/.portable/ per app

What a workspace looks like

<app>/.portable/Consumer Mode
.portable/
├── python/              # interpreter + site-packages
├── scripts/
│   ├── repair.py        # staged from upstream
│   ├── sitecustomize.py
│   └── bin/shim.exe
├── app/                 # app source or compiled artifacts
├── requirements.txt
├── checksums.psd1       # project-local version hashes
└── dist/*.zip           # release package

06Walkthrough: packaging cowsay

Every command and output below comes from a real build: Windows 11, PowerShell 7, embeddable Python 3.14.7, cowsay 6.1.

Create an external workspace

Keep generated files in a temp directory so the repository stays clean; -Workspace also stages the runtime scripts there.

PowerShellRepository root
PS> $ws = "$env:TEMP\cowsay-demo\.portable"
PS> .\scripts\bootstrap.ps1 -Workspace $ws -Engine embeddable `
          -Version 3.14.7 -NonInteractive

Install cowsay

pip.ps1 rewrites cowsay.exe into a shim immediately after the install and writes the .entry sidecar.

PowerShellInstall dependency
PS> .\scripts\pip.ps1 -Workspace $ws install cowsay

Run it two ways

The module route bypasses the launcher; the CLI route goes through the shim. Both should work.

PowerShellRun
PS> & "$ws\python\python.exe" -m cowsay -t "moo from portable env"
PS> & "$ws\python\Scripts\cowsay.exe" -t "hello shim"
  _____________________
| moo from portable env |

                        ^__^
                        (oo)\_______
                        (__)\       )\/\
                            ||----w |
                            ||     ||

  __________
| hello shim |
  ==========
          \

             ^__^

             (__)\       )\/\
                 ||----w |

Inspect the rewritten launcher

No large trampoline and no absolute path: a ~7 KB shim plus a text file describing the entry point.

python\Scripts\Measured files
cowsay.exe      7168 bytes
cowsay.entry      45 bytes

# cowsay.entry
module=cowsay.__main__
func=cli
gui=false

Stage the app and build a ZIP

The runtime convention is <workspace>/app. Application code can import the installed cowsay directly.

app\main.pyApplication entry
import cowsay

def main():
    cowsay.cow("Hello from a portable package")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
PowerShellPackage
PS> .\scripts\build_release.ps1 -Workspace $ws -ReleaseName cowsay-demo

Measured output: 978 files, 5 launchers generated; the ZIP is 15.1 MB.

Run it from another folder

Extract anywhere and run directly. The first start updates python/.portable_root; the launchers are already relative, so nothing manual is needed.

PowerShellAfter relocation
PS> Expand-Archive $zip -DestinationPath "$env:TEMP\cowsay-moved"
PS> cd "$env:TEMP\cowsay-moved"
PS> .\python\python.exe .\app\main.py
PS> .\python\Scripts\cowsay.exe -t "after another move"

| Hello from a portable package |

The embeddable engine's ._pth pins sys.path, so python -m app.main cannot find app inside the package by default. Use python app\main.py, set PYTHONPATH=app, or start through App.exe with app.ini.

Most of site-packages is pip and setuptools; trimming build-time tools would shrink the package further. Compression takes it from 33 MB to 15 MB.

07Limits

ScenarioWhat happensHandling
python -Ssite is skipped, so sitecustomize does not runTrigger repair via activate.ps1 or pip.ps1
A running exeWindows cannot overwrite a running imageSkip now, retry on the next start
Direct uv pip installuv is a separate process and does not fire the exit hookUse pip.ps1, or accept repair on the next start
pip install -eLeaves an absolute path in __editable__*.pthAvoid it, or reinstall after moving
Jupyter kernelspeckernel.json records absolute pathsRe-run ipykernel install after moving
Missing MSVC runtimeNative extensions fail to loadCopy msvcp140.dll and friends into python\

08Compiled artifacts and closed source

The runtime only distributes; it does not compile or encrypt. Cython .pyd files, Nuitka output, and similar artifacts belong to the application build layer. Put them in the staged <workspace>/app and they ship as-is.

  • The Python used for compilation must match the bundled engine's minor version and architecture, or the extension will not load.
  • The embeddable engine ships no headers or import libraries, so it cannot build extensions directly. PBS ships headers and libs/, so compilation and runtime can share one engine.
  • Do not keep the .py source for a protected module in the release; whether sources ship is decided during staging.
If your goal is "users must not read the source", compile or freeze it in your own development environment and hand the output to this runtime. Encryption is not the runtime's job.
